terms:
Effective November 1, 2026. Version 2026-11-01.2. These terms govern station submissions to Radio La Voix Divine, including listings and station-code access on compatible radio devices.

Your authority and required rights

You must be an adult authorized to act for the station. You confirm that you have the rights and permissions needed for the submitted stream, music and other programming, cover art, logos, trademarks, and descriptions, including the territories and uses you authorize. Do not submit a stream you are not authorized to distribute. A publicly accessible stream is not proof of permission. You are responsible for maintaining applicable broadcast, performance, recording, and other licenses and for complying with your streaming provider's terms.

Permission you grant

You grant Radio La Voix Divine a nonexclusive permission, for operation of this service, to store, reproduce, resize, cache, display and distribute your submitted name, artwork and descriptions on the website and compatible radios, and to supply your stream URL and updates to radios so listeners can connect directly to the station. You authorize service providers acting for us to perform those functions. You retain your rights. This permission does not give us rights in underlying music or other third-party content you do not control.

Station codes and editing

A station code (2-6 digits) is public and can be shared with listeners. It is not a password. Keep the private email sign-in link confidential. You must keep your station information and contact email accurate. Request withdrawal or a contact correction through the privacy/contact form. We may require evidence that you control the station before making sensitive changes.

Review and prohibited submissions

Do not submit unauthorized streams, misleading impersonations, malware, scams, illegal content or unlawful threats. Approval and a station code do not certify that we verified your licenses or endorse your content. We may request evidence of authority and rights, reject a submission, or suspend/remove access while investigating rights, safety or legal concerns.

Complaints, repeat infringement and withdrawal

Use our Copyright & complaints page to report a rights concern. We review notices and may disable listings, artwork and code lookups. We will terminate submission access for repeat infringers in appropriate circumstances and reasonably implement that policy, considering notices, evidence and disputes rather than treating an accusation alone as a final infringement finding. Existing independent streams or cached data on offline or older radios may remain accessible; we do not control a third party's stream server.

Optional local sponsor messages

Businesses may submit advertisements to a selected station for compatible radios playing that station. The station owner must approve each ad; flagged content also requires administrator clearance. You confirm permission to advertise the business and to use its images, trademarks and claims, and authorize us to screen, resize, store and display that material. Keep claims accurate and comply with applicable advertising requirements. Submitted ads remain paused until the station owner approves them. We may pause or reject ads for safety, rights or service reasons. The current pilot has no fee or automatic billing; any future paid plan requires a separate, explicit purchase. Device-reported displays do not establish human attention, audience size or sales, and no advertising results are promised.

Availability and responsibility

Streams and third-party services may change or stop. We do not promise uninterrupted access, a particular audience, earnings or continued placement. To the extent permitted by law, you agree to be responsible for losses and third-party claims caused by your breach of this agreement or unauthorized submissions. Nothing here excludes liability or consumer rights that cannot lawfully be excluded. This agreement does not create a partnership or transfer ownership of your station.

Privacy and changes

Our Privacy notice explains handling of contact information and submission records. We record the agreement version and acceptance time. Materially revised submission terms require renewed acceptance for new submissions or station updates; earlier records are not treated as acceptance of a later version.
privacy:
Effective October 29, 2026. This notice covers Radio La Voix Divine's station directory, registration, editing and optional radio-linking tools. Radio-linking information was updated October 30, 2026. Content-screening information was updated October 31, 2026. Local sponsor-ad information was added November 1, 2026.

What we collect and make public

Registration collects station name, stream URL, artwork, bio, location and contact email. Station information, artwork, stream URLs and listener codes may be publicly displayed or delivered to radios. Contact emails, sign-in secrets, rights-request details and acceptance records are not published in Library or the device API.

Website analytics

We use Cloudflare Web Analytics on public browsing pages to understand visits, page views and page performance. Your browser sends performance measurements to Cloudflare. We do not install this analytics beacon on administrator, station-editor or phone-linking pages. Website visits are separate from radio-device listening activity.

Bot protection

When enabled, Cloudflare Turnstile checks station submissions and email-code requests to help prevent automated abuse. Your browser connects to Cloudflare for this security check. We send the verification token to Cloudflare for validation; we do not send station email addresses, station content or uploaded artwork as part of that validation.

Local sponsor messages on radios

Business advertisers submit business names, offers, public business phone numbers, artwork and requested schedules, plus a private contact name and email. We share those contact details with the selected station owner and site administrators to review and handle the submission. Contact email addresses are not verified and are not displayed on radios. Ads cleared by safety screening and approved by the station owner may be displayed on compatible radios playing that station. We record the advertiser’s permission confirmation and create short-lived, device-scoped delivery receipts. A device can report that it displayed an ad; we keep aggregate counts for the station and use a private random radio identifier to enforce delivery limits and prevent duplicate counts. Owners see aggregate counts, not radio credentials or individual device identifiers. This does not track whether a person actually saw an ad. Delivery receipts are cleaned up after seven days when the service is used. Campaigns and permissions are retained for service operation and safety review; deleted material may remain in private records/backups. No payment-card information is collected during the free pilot.

Monthly active-radio preview

Updated radios report the selected station after one minute of continuous playback over their authenticated connection. We count each radio once per station per calendar month in New York time. Monthly station-specific hashes distinguish reports without showing device identifiers to station owners. We retain the current and previous twelve calendar months of these records; older records are removed when new activity is recorded. These reports are not verified counts of people and older firmware is not included. Proposed station-plan prices are informational only; billing and automatic plan enforcement are not active.

Automatic content screening

We check station names, titles, bios, sponsor messages and artwork for prohibited content. When automatic artwork screening is connected, submitted text and artwork are sent to OpenAI for screening. Contact emails, private sign-in codes and radio credentials are not sent for content screening. Flagged content and unavailable scans are held for administrator review. Automated checks can make mistakes; contact us to request review.

How we use information

We use it to operate the directory, deliver requested station codes and sign-in emails, update stations, prevent abuse and investigate rights or privacy requests. We store the agreement version, its text hash, station reference and acceptance time. Requests and administrative decisions are retained privately for follow-up and accountability.

Optional phone-to-radio linking

If you link a phone, we store a random radio identifier, a hash of its private credential, last connection time, temporary pairing requests and phone permission records. Linking requires approval on the radio. A browser cookie remembers that permission for up to 30 days. Station-add requests expire after five minutes; their records and pairing-request records are cleaned up after seven days when the service is used. These tools do not collect your home Wi-Fi password. Both devices communicate with our hosting service over encrypted connections. Use Unlink phones on the radio to revoke access, and clear browser cookies to forget this browser. A restored backup requires fresh phone approval.

Browser storage and logs

Essential session cookies support forms, admin authentication and private station editing. Your browser may store your language and an identifier used for listening statistics. The site can record listening duration and station/session information. Hosting/security logs can include IP addresses, request times, browser information and requested pages. Limits used to prevent repeated requests may store a hash of an IP address or email. Browser controls let you clear cookies/storage, although forms and sign-in may stop working.

Service providers and third parties

Hosting, email delivery and security providers process data to operate the service. Playing a stream or loading external artwork/news can connect your browser or radio to a third-party provider, which receives connection information and applies its own policies. Requests may be disclosed where reasonably needed to investigate a complaint, comply with law or protect rights; we avoid unnecessarily sharing private contact details.

Retention and security

Station records are kept while operating the listing. Private station-editing sessions expire after 30 minutes. Older sign-in links expire after 30 minutes. New editing and registration email verification codes expire after 15 minutes; we store a keyed hash and an encrypted email-delivery copy until verification or expiry. We retain agreement and complaint records as needed for service operation, disputes, security and legal obligations, then review them for deletion. Backups and hosting/email logs may retain earlier copies. We use restricted admin access, HTTPS, session controls and private databases; no system can guarantee absolute security. Do not include unnecessary sensitive information in submissions or requests.

Your requests

Use the Privacy/contact form to request access, correction or deletion, or withdraw a station. We verify identity before releasing private records or changing a listing. Some information may be retained where needed to address a dispute or legal obligation. Do not send passwords, financial information or identification documents through this form.

Radio controls, software and support updates — November 7, 2026

Compatible radios report their software version, selected station, volume, mute state and the time of the latest report through an authenticated connection. These details are shown only to linked phones. Remote station selection, volume and mute require a separate approval on the physical radio; an existing station-add permission does not automatically enable controls. Control requests expire after one minute, and records are removed after seven days. Unlinking or resetting the Device Code revokes the relevant permissions. The website does not receive the home Wi-Fi password.

Support submissions and replies are stored privately for follow-up. The submitting browser may view its ticket for 30 minutes. Another browser must verify a private email code before viewing that ticket. Codes expire after 15 minutes, have a maximum of five attempts and work once; private ticket access expires after 30 minutes. These temporary grants and challenges are not included in backups and are revoked on restore. We do not publish support messages, email addresses or device codes.

Language and larger-text settings are saved locally as display preferences. Unfinished forms remain in memory; a website update waits until they are finished. A deliberate safe refresh may preserve only a public station search and scroll position in session storage for up to one minute. Form contents, device codes, files and sign-in codes are not stored by this update feature.
copyright:
Use the form below to report suspected infringement or another rights concern involving a station listing, artwork or stream link. We store reports privately for administrator review. A report is not an automatic infringement finding.

Copyright notices

Identify the copyrighted work and the specific material or link you believe infringes it; include the station code or listing location, your contact details, an electronic signature, and the good-faith and authority statements below. Incomplete reports may require follow-up. Misrepresentations can have legal consequences. Relevant notice details may be shared with the affected station where needed to address a claim or as required by law.

Review and repeat infringement

Our administrator reviews requests, may request evidence, and may suspend listings or artwork while investigating. Repeat infringers may have all their listings disabled and future submission access terminated in appropriate circumstances. We record decisions; do not assume a request has been resolved solely because the form was submitted.

Disputes and counter-notices

If material was removed due to a copyright notice and you believe that was a mistake or misidentification, use the Counter-notice page. Applicable DMCA procedures can require forwarding a valid counter-notice and restoring material in 10–14 business days unless the claimant reports a court action. An administrator must review the notice and the applicable procedure; restoration is not automatic.

Contact channel and designated-agent status

This form is an operational complaint channel. It is not a representation that a DMCA designated agent has been registered or that the service qualifies for a statutory safe harbor. A designated agent's registered name, address, telephone and email must be supplied and published separately if that process is used.

Logo credits

counter-notice: Use this only when material was removed following a copyright complaint and you believe the removal resulted from a mistake or misidentification. A counter-notice can have legal consequences. Consider legal advice before submitting. A valid counter-notice includes your signature, identification and previous location of the removed material, your contact details, and the sworn statement and jurisdiction/service-of-process consent below. Relevant information, including your contact details, may need to be forwarded to the original complainant.
